title: Wednesday Afternoon Book Club  - Online Option
description: Discover new fiction book titles and connect with like-minded readers for animated discussions. Please note that the online version of this book club connects you directly with the in-person meeting.
long_description:
To Register - Click on "Register" button on the left

Book Clubs are led by the community members that attend on a regular basis, they select the monthly books in advance so everyone can read the same book title. This book club meets the first Wednesday of the month, from September to May.

Listed below are a few reminders so everyone can enjoy the club: 

  • The safety of our participants and staff is our top priority, please review our Patron Conduct Policy.
  • Registration is required, space is limited. If you cannot attend, please cancel your registration.
  • All participants are encouraged to read the book, if you don't like the style, at least read the first few chapters and the final chapter so you can participate in the discussions.
  • Remember to stay on topic, you invested the time to read the book, so come prepared to discuss. There are no wrong or right interpretations of a book ? just different perspectives.
  • Be gracious in your comments. If you did not like the book, be kind in your feedback. Contribute positively and respectfully.
  • Take turns, give everyone a chance to share. Remember, book clubs are discussion groups. Keep an open mind, ready to discover new books and ideas. 
  • Respect the discussion space, be a good listener and don't engage in side conversations, be sure to mute your cell phones!

Book Club Selections

September 2nd - The Briar Club by Kate Quinn

October 7th - How to Survive a Bear Attack by Claire Cameron

November 4th - My Friends by Fredrik Backman

December 2nd - TBD

January 6th - Pillars of the Earth by Ken Follett

February 3rd - Demon Copperhead by Barbara Kingsolver

March 3rd - The Book Club for Troublesome Women by Marie Bostwick

April 7th - Girl on a Platform by Ellie Millwood *Note this book is not in our library collection

May 5th - Theo the Golden by Allen Levi

June 2nd - Book selection for next year 

If you are unable to attend, we ask that you cancel your registration or email askus@barrielibrary.ca

Questions? Please call 705-728-1010 or email askus@barrielibrary.ca

We want to improve, to serve you better. Please take a moment to complete our Program Evaluation Form.

title: Simcoe Reads
description: Eight Libraries. Eight Books. One Winner. Join us at the John Hayter Southshore Community Centre see who will take home the title of Simcoe Reads 2026 Champion this year!
long_description:
Location - General John Hayter Southshore Community Centre.

    Eight Libraries. Eight Books. 1 Winner.

    Based on Canada Reads, 8 Simcoe County Libraries have each selected a Canadian book and a local celebrity to champion it. On this night, we will all gather to chat about our books and why we think Simcoe County should read them. Come and enjoy the discussion and in the end you, our amazing audience, will vote to decide which book will be crowned the 2026 Simcoe Reads winner. 

    The Simcoe County libraries are squaring off in this years cover-to-cover discussion are: Barrie, Bradford West Gwillimbury, Essa, Innisfil, Midland, New Tecumseth, Ramara and Severn.

    Can't make it in person: The event will also be streaming live via Zoom. Click here to register and receive a link to the online edition of this event.

    To learn more about Simcoe Reads, please visit: 

    • Our Simcoe Reads 2026 website
    • Previous Simcoe Reads picks

    Please note:

    • Barrie Residents - Parking is free with your Digital Waterfront Pass. To learn more about Barrie Waterfront Passes, click here.
    • Non-Barrie Residents - A number of free spaces have been allotted to you so you can enjoy the event too! Once these spaces are filled, parking rates will apply.

    We ask that all participants conduct themselves respectfully, and adhere to the Patron Conduct Policy.

    If you have any questions or require technical assistance please call 705-728-1010 or email askus@barrielibrary.ca

title: The Librarians: Film Screening & Discussion
sub_title: Ontario Public Library Week Special Event
description: Join BPL staff and supporters for a free public screening of The Librarians documentary, along with an open conversation on libraries and freedom of expression.
long_description:
The Librarians is a documentary film that debuted at Sundance Film Festival in 2025, directed and produced by Kim A. Snyder: "As an unprecedented wave of book banning is sparked in Texas, Florida, and beyond, librarians under siege join forces as unlikely defenders fighting for intellectual freedom on the front lines of democracy."

Join us at the Georgian Theatre for a free screening of the film, alongside a wide-ranging discussion with library professionals on challenges faced by public libraries and how best to support freedom of expression in your community. 

Tickets are free but registration is required! Please click 'REGISTER' to reserve free seats for you and your friends. 

Event Details

Doors Open: 5:45pm

Discussion: 6:00pm

Showtime: 6:30pm 

From 6-6:30pm, members of the Barrie Public Library leadership team will be having an open conversation about freedom of expression, the current landscape in Canada, as well as how libraries serve our diverse communities. Audience Q&A will take place if time allows.

The Librarians documentary screening will begin at 6:30pm (1h32m run time) 

Learn more about The Librarians. 

Please note that paid parking is required at Georgian Theatre.

title: AccessOAP Support Sessions
description: Sit down with a Regional Service Network Specialist from AccessOAP to receive support with registration, expense support for Core Clinical Services, and answers to general AccessOAP questions.
long_description:
Register for a 30-minute in-person appointment with a Regional Service Network Specialist from AccessOAP. 

Select an appointment time from the Registration drop-down menu. 

For appointments related to first-time registration with AccessOAP, families will be required to provide 3 documents as proof of age, residency, and diagnosis during the registration process. Please bring this documentation to your appointment. Please see below for acceptable documentation.

Proof of Age (one of the following):

  • birth certificate
  • proof of live birth
  • valid passport (not expired for more than 5 years)
  • valid permanent resident card (not expired for more than 5 years)

Residency Verification (one of the following):

  • school report card
  • primary caregiver's driver's license or identification card
  • piece of mail

Proof of Diagnosis (document must include all of the following):

  • child's full name and date of birth
  • date of the child's assessment
  • a statement confirming the child meets the diagnostic criteria for Autism Spectrum Disorder
  • qualified professional's name and credentials
